summary: Light on North Dumpling Island, Fishers Island Sound: established 1849, rebuilt 1871, automated 1959; private island, closed to visitors.

structures.note: 29 ft (8.8 m) tower and lantern on the dwelling after the 1871 rebuild (LighthouseFriends); the archive gives 39.5 ft from base to lantern centre

access.note: Privately owned island. Grounds, dwelling and tower closed. Do not land. Best seen from the water; excursion boats pass it (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Private owner. LighthouseFriends names Dean Kamen as owner from 1986 (2003 report).

corrections.why: The tower standing today dates from the 1871 rebuild: the archive gives the tower as established 1871, and LighthouseFriends describes a new tower and lantern on the dwelling in 1871. The 1849 structure was the brick dwelling with a 25-foot tower (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.proposed: Fifth-order lens installed 1892, replacing a sixth-order lens (21 July 1892)
corrections.why: The Board's report for the year ended 30 June 1893 records a change from sixth to fifth order on 21 July 1892; LighthouseFriends agrees. The archive's 1871 fifth-order entry is not supported by these sources.

corrections.proposed: F W with a fixed red sector (set 1891)
corrections.why: The 1891 change to fixed white with a fixed red sector is recorded in the Board's report and in the Tribune's notice to mariners. Whether the red sector remains today is not confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station was established in 1849 (archive). The 1871 date is the rebuilt tower and lantern (archive, LighthouseFriends). Both are first years of different structures.

The archive's fifth-order original optic of 1871 conflicts with the Board's 1893 report, which records a sixth-order lens replaced by a fifth-order lens in July 1892. The Board's report is followed here; the archive's 1871 entry is left unresolved in the story.

notes_for_editor: 1) Focal height: the record's 28.7 m (ENC) is not matched by the archive (69.25 ft above mean high water, 21.1 m, used here). Not resolved further. 2) Tower height: the story uses 29 ft (LighthouseFriends); the archive gives 39.5 ft to lantern centre; the record's 9.4 m is not supported by a source read here. 3) Status: the archive says not an active aid to navigation; other records disagree on whether it still shows; not settled in the story. 4) Current optic: the archive gives a 300 mm optic (a fifth-order size); whether it is in place today is unverified; LighthouseFriends says the optic went back on the tower in 1977. 5) OCR items to check on the page image: LHB FY1892 scan 76 prints 'Forth Dumpling' (read as North Dumpling); LHB FY1893 scan 78 prints 'Fanck lamps' (Funck lamps); Commissioner scan 66 (J. J. Barnes) was checked on the page image on 2026-10-27: it is the rates-of-life-and-property-saved table for FY1915 (printed p.61, heading 'Saving of life and property'), so the story no longer calls it a keeper table; Bulletin 1934 p.21 prints 'Fricks' (archive: Fricke); Bulletin 1938 p.40 was checked on the page image: the list reads Latimer Reef, North Dumpling, Race Rock, Little Gull Island and Orient Point. The LHB FY1892 'Forth Dumpling' (scan 76) was not image-checked. 6) Date conflict for the 1891 characteristic change: Board report 16 October; Tribune notice 'on or about October 15'; LighthouseFriends 15 October. Both kept in the story. 7) Name variants: Burkhardt is 1916-1930 in the archive but 'at least 1917' in LighthouseFriends; John Baker is 'John Baker III' in LighthouseFriends; Fricke is printed 'Fricks' in the 1934 Bulletin. 8) Anecdotes sourced only to LighthouseFriends (no primary in the corpus or newspapers read): Riley Clark, Joseph Dayton, the steamboat fog-bell refusal, the 1899 bell and Board letter, the 1902 telephone, the 1923 rum-running accusation, the 1959 and 1977 sale prices, and Kamen. Reported as LighthouseFriends' account. A check against the 1899-1900 Board correspondence or newspapers would firm them up. 9) Chronicling America 'North Dumpling' search (1847-1960) returned mostly unrelated pages; only the 1891 Tribune notice is used. 10) Not checked: NRHP status; any Board report before 1891 (the corpus starts there), so the 1849 establishment, the 1855 sixth-order lens and the 1871 rebuild rest on the archive and LighthouseFriends; the 1838 Bache survey and 1847 appropriation rest on LighthouseFriends. 11) The Johnson (1889) fog-trial passage gives no year; it concerns the waters around this station, not the station's own signal. 12) Wikipedia was read for leads only; nothing in this file cites it. 13) Fact-check 2026-10-27: the unsourced statement that other records disagree on whether the light still shows was removed; the 1923 accusation now follows LighthouseFriends' wording; the Johnson fog-trial passage now says the Little Gull siren was heard at the North Dumpling station.
